messages:
sophia: hey team — i have a customer report with an X-Request-ID: 0a1b2c3d. they say generation failed, but console search returns nothing. where do i start?
jamie: do you have a trace_id too or just the X-Request-ID? sometimes edge strips the header and the trace is the only clue.
sophia: only the header in the payload, no trace in the error report. it came from the embeddings route (/v1/embeddings).
alex: quick checklist: 1) check edge/access-logs for that x-req header 2) follow the request to proxy pod -> model pod 3) if console hides the field use stern on ingress or query logs by client_ip+time window.
morgan: console quick query (use quotes):
```
logs query: "X-Request-ID=\"0a1b2c3d\"" | sort @timestamp desc | limit 50
```
if console redacts it, try the raw logs index: logs_raw-*-2023 or the ingress index.
jamie: CLI fallback (on mac/linux):
```
kubectl -n ingress get pods -l app=edge -o name | xargs -I{} kubectl logs {} --since=30m | rg "0a1b2c3d"
```
also try stern if you want live tail across pods:
```
stern edge -n ingress -c edge-proxy --since 1m | rg "0a1b2c3d"
```
sophia: trying the kubectl approach now. any chance a trace could exist without the header? ops-bot: note: sampled traces may omit headers, but trace_id often makes it through if tracing is enabled.
jamie: if you find a span, open tracing UI -> search by trace_id -> there is a link to correlated logs (bottom-left). that page shows pod and container names — good jump point for kubectl/stern.
alex: other trick: if the customer included a timestamp, search logs by service name + approximate time window, then look for requests with matching latency/error code and correlate.
morgan: if you hit rate-limited consoles, use the internal search API (auth required):
```
POST https://internal-search.redwood/api/v1/logs/query
body: {"q":"service:embeddings AND status:500 AND @timestamp:[2023-05-01T15:00 TO 2023-05-01T15:05]"}
```
jamie: also check this common gotcha: some older proxies rewrite X-Request-ID to X-Req-Ref. try both keys in your grep.
sophia: found an entry in ingress logs that references span=abcd1234, but no payload. moving to tracing UI now.
alex: nice. once you have trace_id, run: `rls traces get <trace_id>` or open //tracing.redwood/trace/<trace_id> (internal) — it shows hop list and links to raw logs.
morgan: if you land on pod logs and still no payload, check if request body was dropped by a filter (nginx lua) — look for "body_buffered" flags in the edge logs.
sophia: opened trace, seeing a model pod error: OOM at generation start. i can pull pod logs. should i escalate to eng-runtime?
jamie: @alex can you triage runtime OOM? likely need to bump memory or change batching. :eyes:
alex: on it — grabbing logs + config. if it's batch size, we can apply a hotfix to lower batch or pin to a quantized variant.
sophia: thanks all. logging my findings in the ticket and i'll post the final pod log snippet here for records. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy-bot: new run queued for runtime-hotfix (PR #1247) triggered by @alex.
